chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareez, from Abu al-Jaroud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) went to Umm Salama, and said to her: 'Why is it that I do not see the blessing in your house?' She said: 'Yes indeed, and praise be to God, for the blessing is certainly in my house.'
So he said: 'Indeed, God, Mighty and Majestic, sent down three blessings: water, fire, and the sheep.'

key_terms.أَنْزَلَ: Anzala — sent down, revealed, bestowed; often used for divine bestowal of gifts or revelation
key_terms.الشَّاة: Al-shaat — the sheep or goat; in Islamic law and culture a central animal for sacrifice, food, and wool provision
key_terms.الْبَرَكَة: Baraka — divine blessing, spiritual and material abundance flowing from God's grace; a quality that multiplies the good in a thing

ai.seo_question: What are the three blessings God sent down according to the Prophet Muhammad?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) narrates that the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) visited his wife Umm Salama and remarked on not perceiving blessing in her household. She affirmed its presence with gratitude. The Prophet then revealed a profound theological teaching: that God sent down three elemental blessings — water, fire, and the sheep — each serving as a foundational gift sustaining human life and worship. This hadith underscores the Islamic concept of baraka (divine blessing) as present in everyday providential gifts, particularly the sheep which provides food, clothing, and sacrifice.
